screening_results.reason: This is an empirical VBM structural MRI study comparing cocaine-dependent (stimulant users) and healthy controls with whole-brain analyses. Multiple between-group contrasts (HC > CD and CD > HC) were modelled and inference was conducted over the whole brain with cluster-level FWE correction. Participant demographics, sex composition, age, and substance-use characteristics (years of cocaine use, abstinence status, urine toxicology) are reported; preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, New Segment, DARTEL) is reported. These features satisfy the review’s requirement for whole-brain voxelwise GM volume comparisons between substance users and controls and acceptable reporting of methods/results. No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only or non-empirical) apply. Full-text is available as represented by the NeuroStore record.

This is an empirical structural MRI study comparing gray-matter volume between methamphetamine-dependent participants and healthy controls (stimulant class). The NeuroStore extraction documents multiple whole-brain between-group contrasts (Analysis 22445480_analysis_0 omnibus; Analysis 22445480_analysis_1 Control Nonsmoker > Methamphetamine-Dependent Tobacco Smoker; Analysis 22445480_analysis_3 Control Tobacco Smoker > Methamphetamine-Dependent Tobacco Smoker) with voxelwise peaks reported in tables. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, and methods are reported. Therefore the study satisfies I2 (empirical MRI GM comparisons), I3 (reports whole-brain between-group contrasts), I4 (voxelwise results available/reported), and I5 (participant and scanner/usage details present). No exclusion criteria (E5 ROI-only or E6 non-empirical) apply.

The NeuroStore extraction indicates all reported voxelwise models were fit over regions of interest (shared field: 'Model fit over: region of interest'), and the paper’s analyses are ROI-based despite mentioning VBM in the abstract. Therefore there is no qualifying whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported, so exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing GM between substance users and controls) and I4 (voxelwise results reported in tables/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast reported). Note: participant age/sex are reported but MRI field strength/preprocessing software are not fully detailed (I5 is preferred and not required).

This is an empirical human structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) study examining gray matter volume differences between nicotine-dependent smokers and non-smokers. NeuroStore metadata indicate whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference (FWE-corrected clusters) with reported peak coordinates/tables, and participant demographics and smoking variables are provided. Although MRI field strength and preprocessing software are not explicitly listed in the record, the review’s criteria allow missing methodological details alone not to exclude a study. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets the inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical human structural MRI VBM study comparing heroin-dependent patients to healthy controls (opioid class), reporting whole-brain between-group contrasts (model fit over whole brain) with reported peak coordinates (Table 1). Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics are reported. The study therefore meets the review objective and required inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM volume comparisons. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Some preprocessing/MRI field-strength/software details are not shown in this record, but the inclusion rules allow missing preferred details. Hence include.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using optimized voxel-based morphometry comparing cocaine-dependent (stimulant) subjects with healthy controls. The paper reports a whole-brain between-group VBM contrast (model fit and inference over the whole brain) with reported peak coordinates and corrected results, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Participant demographics and clinical assessment (age, sex, DSM-IV/SCID) and VBM methods are described. Therefore the study meets the review objective (stimulant users) and all required inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM volume comparisons. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) apply.

This study reports within-group voxelwise correlations between alcohol dependence severity (ADS) and gray matter density in heavy drinking smokers (n=39) but does not include any between-group contrasts comparing substance users to non-using controls. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (participant age/sex and substance use characteristics are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (does not assess GM volume differences between substance users and controls), I3 (does not report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls). I4 is not applicable because the reported voxelwise peaks are for within-group associations rather than qualifying between-group results. No exclusion criteria from the list apply (e.g., this is not an ROI-only paper nor a non-empirical paper). Therefore the paper must be excluded for failing required between-group inclusion criteria.

The NeuroStore record indicates all reported analyses were region-of-interest (model fit and inference restricted to ROI; region-level thresholding) with no whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrasts. This violates the requirement for whole-brain results, so the study meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language structural MRI study assessing GM volume differences between substance users and controls) and I5 (participant age/sex and substance use characteristics are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM volume contrasts reported). Full text appears available in the record; fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study reports a whole-brain voxel-based morphometry contrast comparing current smokers vs nonsmokers (nicotine users vs controls) with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates. Participant demographics (age, sex), clinical measures, and analysis details are provided in the NeuroStore record. This satisfies the review objective (nicotine class) and inclusion criteria for empirical GM volume comparisons with whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical (human) VBM MRI study comparing smokers (nicotine-dependent) and nonsmokers, reporting whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (nonsmokers > smokers) with reported peak coordinates (Table 2) and a whole-brain model fit. Participant demographics and substance-use measures are provided. Thus it meets the review objective (nicotine) and inclusion criteria: I2 (empirical MRI GM comparison), I3 (at least one whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast), and I4 (results reported in tables of coordinates). Some technical details (MRI field strength, preprocessing/software) are not listed in this record, but I5 is a preferred (not mandatory) item and absence of those details does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical VBM study comparing former heroin-dependent (opioid) users to non-addicted controls, reporting whole-brain between-group GM volume analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain; Analysis 0: FHD > CN) with reported peak coordinates. Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics are provided. Resting-state connectivity analyses are additional but do not negate the structural whole-brain VBM result. The study therefore meets criteria I2 (empirical English MRI GM comparison), I3 (reports at least one whole-brain between-group GM contrast), I4 (voxelwise results reported in tables/peaks), and I5 (reports age/sex and substance-use details). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears available in the provided record.

This is an empirical human MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing smokers (nicotine-dependent) and matched non-smoking controls (n=88). It reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (non-smoking controls > smokers) of gray matter volume with coordinate peaks (Talairach), thresholding and cluster extent—thus providing whole-brain GM volume results suitable for meta-analysis. Participant age/sex and smoking characteristics are reported; MRI field strength and preprocessing software are not listed but the protocol allows missing details. No ROI-only or non-empirical exclusion criteria apply. Therefore all required inclusion conditions for this review are met.

This is an empirical human MRI voxel-based morphometry study comparing gray matter volume between cocaine-dependent patients and matched healthy controls. It reports at least one whole-brain between-group contrast (controls > cocaine group) with model fit and inference performed over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence. Participant demographics and substance-use measures (age, sex, years of use, DSM-IV diagnosis) are provided. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM comparison), I3 (whole-brain between-group contrast), I4 (results reported as peaks/tables), and I5 (participant and substance-use details reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text is available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The record reports an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol dependent patients (ADPs) and healthy controls with a whole-brain voxelwise GM volume contrast (HCs > ADPs). Results are FWE-corrected across the whole volume (voxel-level p<0.05) and peaks are reported in a table. The model and covariates are described and participant/sample characteristics are reported. This satisfies the meta-analysis objective (GM differences in substance users vs controls). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not non-empirical).

This is an empirical VBM study comparing heroin-dependent individuals (opioid users) to healthy controls reporting whole-brain between-group contrasts (Controls > HDI) with voxelwise analyses and coordinate peaks. The study addresses the review objective (opioid class). NeuroStore record indicates whole-brain model fitting and inference, cluster- and FDR-thresholded results, and reported coordinate peaks (tables). Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics are reported. MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not specified in the record (I5 preferred but not required). No ROI-only or non-empirical exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets required inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion.

This study investigates cocaine dependence (a stimulant), reports an empirical structural MRI analysis of gray matter volume, and presents a whole-brain between-group contrast (HC > CD) with coordinate peaks (20 peaks) and whole-brain inference. Participant demographics (age, sex) and clinical details are reported. While MRI field strength and preprocessing/software aren’t provided in the record, I5 is stated as preferred and missing details alone should not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the review objective and key inclusion criteria.

Excluded because the study reports cortical thickness (structural morphometry) measures rather than grey matter volume/density/concentration as required by inclusion criterion I2. The paper does provide whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (meets I3) and reports coordinate peaks/tables (meets I4); participant demographics and substance-use details and preprocessing software (FreeSurfer) are reported. No exclusion criteria (E5 or E6) are met. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I2 (GM volume/density) despite satisfying other inclusion criteria.

Excluded because the study only reports morphometric results with inference restricted to a region-of-interest using small-volume correction (FWE SVC) and does not report any qualifying whole-brain voxelwise GM volume between-group results. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (ROI-only reporting with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language MRI study assessing GM volume differences between substance users and controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no reported whole-brain between-group GM volume contrast; morphometry inference restricted to ROI). I5 (full reporting of MRI field strength) is not fully met (field strength not reported), though age/sex, substance-use details, and analysis software (SPM8) are provided. Full text appears complete in this record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The NeuroStore record describes an empirical VBM study of smokers vs. never-smokers (meets I2) and reports participant demographics and substance-use measures (meets I5). However, the analysis was performed and inference restricted to an a priori cerebellum/brainstem region using the SUIT toolbox (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest). No whole-brain between-group GM contrast is reported. This violates the review's whole-brain requirement, so exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only study with no qualifying whole-brain results) applies. Therefore the study is excluded.

This is an original empirical human structural MRI VBM study comparing cocaine-dependent participants (n=60) with healthy controls (n=60) reporting grey matter volume differences. The abstract explicitly reports extensive decreases and focal increases in GM volume between groups, and NeuroStore notes a between-group difference map (ROI defined by between-group analysis) and MNI coordinate space. The report also provides participant age/sex and substance-use characteristics. Although the NeuroStore-extracted voxelwise analyses are within-group regressions using an ROI, the presence of a between-group GM map and whole-brain VBM language in the abstract satisfy the requirement for whole-brain between-group contrasts (I3). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical human structural MRI (VBM) study comparing gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls (n=22 AD, n=21 HC; total n=43). It reports at least one whole-brain between-group contrast (HC > AD) with voxel-wise FWE-corrected results and reported peak(s). Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics (age, sex, abstinence duration, duration of dependence) are reported. The study is not ROI-only and is original empirical data. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study reports structural MRI comparisons between heroin users and controls (meets I2) and provides voxelwise results available in the document (meets I4). Participant and study details are reported (meets I5). However, the NeuroStore extraction specifies that the morphometric model was fit over and inference was restricted to a region of interest (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest). Therefore the paper does not provide a qualifying whole-brain between-group contrast and falls under exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. Full text is considered complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical structural MRI study comparing gray matter (gray matter density) between heroin-dependent (opioid) participants and healthy controls using whole-brain voxelwise morphometry. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (healthy > heroin) after 3 days and 1 month abstinence with coordinate peaks listed (tables). Participant demographics and substance use details are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria: I2 (empirical MRI GM differences), I3 (whole-brain between-group contrasts), I4 (voxelwise results/coordinates reported), and I5 (participant age/sex and substance use characteristics reported; MRI field strength/software not reported but this alone does not exclude). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing gray matter volume between experienced amphetamine-type stimulant (ATS) users (a stimulant class relevant to the review) and control groups. The NeuroStore record shows voxelwise whole-brain VBM analyses with whole-brain inference and permutation-based FWE-corrected cluster-level results (reported peaks/tables and figures) demonstrating GM volume reductions in experienced users versus low-exposure and drug-naive controls. Participant demographics and substance-use group definitions are reported. These facts satisfy inclusion criteria I2 (empirical English MRI study of GM differences), I3 (reports at least one whole-brain between-group GM contrast), I4 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures), and I5 (participant age/sex and substance-use characteristics provided). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be included.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing gray matter volume between stimulant-using participants and controls. It reports a whole-brain between-group contrast (Analysis 1: users vs controls) with model fit and inference over the whole brain and provides reported peak coordinates (table). Participant age/sex and substance-use characteristics are reported. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective (stimulants). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical).

The study is an empirical human VBM MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent patients to healthy controls and reports whole-brain voxelwise gray-matter and white-matter contrasts. NeuroStore extraction shows model fit and inference were performed over the whole brain, voxel-level FDR thresholding, and peak coordinates are reported in Table 1/2 — satisfying the acceptability of coordinates reporting. Participant demographics and substance-use details (n, ages, sex, drinking history, abstinence) are provided. Alcohol is one of the target substance classes. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

This study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) voxelwise analyses: 'Model fit over: region of interest' and 'Inference restricted to: region of interest' with small-volume FWE correction. Therefore it does not provide any whole-brain between-group GM contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study comparing GM volume between substance users and controls) and I5 (participant age/sex and some substance-use characteristics reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast reported). No indication of E6. Based on the absence of whole-brain results required by I3, the study is excluded.

This empirical VBM study compares gray matter density between heroin-dependent individuals and healthy controls, reporting a whole-brain between-group contrast (healthy > addiction) with thresholded results and reported peak coordinates (Table tbl2). Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM comparisons), I3 (whole-brain between-group voxelwise results), I4 (coordinates/results reported), and I5 (participant and substance-use details reported). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record.

This VBM study reports whole-brain between-group gray-matter comparisons of nicotine-dependent smokers versus healthy non-smokers, with coordinates/peaks reported in tables. It is an empirical human MRI study addressing nicotine (one of the five drug classes of interest). NeuroStore extraction shows model fit and inference over the whole brain for GM contrasts and reports peak coordinates in tables, and participant age/sex and substance-use characteristics are provided. These features satisfy the review’s core inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text is available as represented by the NeuroStore record.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing gray matter volume between substance-dependent patients (cocaine and heroin) and healthy controls. NeuroStore extraction indicates whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (cocaine<controls; heroin<controls) with reported coordinates (peaks in table), appropriate group ANCOVA models, and participant demographics (sample sizes, mean ages, years of abuse). These satisfy the review’s requirement for empirical GM volume comparisons and whole-brain between-group results; voxelwise results are reported in tables, which is acceptable. Some reporting details (e.g., sex distribution, MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not provided in the extracted record, but the protocol states missing such details alone should not exclude a qualifying study. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply.

This study is excluded because it compares two subgroups of dependent smokers (relapsers vs quitters) rather than substance users versus non-user controls. Inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM differences between substance users and controls) and I3 (whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls) are NOT met. The study does report whole-brain voxelwise morphometric results with peak coordinates in Table 2 (satisfying I4) and reports substance-use covariates (years smoked, cigarettes/day) and sex as covariates (partially satisfying I5). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears available in the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical VBM study comparing nicotine-dependent individuals (NDs) to healthy controls (n=160) and reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (NDs<Controls and NDs>Controls) with coordinate peaks and cluster-level FWE correction. The abstract and extracted analyses state whole-brain model fitting and inference, report preprocessing software (SPM8/DARTEL), participant sex and smoking characteristics, and results in tables. These features satisfy the review objective (nicotine users vs controls) and meet inclusion criteria I2, I3, and I4; sufficient participant/method details are provided (I5). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, empirical human MRI data).

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing gray matter volumes between detoxified alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls. The abstract and NeuroStore extraction report whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM decreases (peaks reported in Table 3), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain between-group GM contrasts; voxelwise results are available in tables/figures. Although some preprocessing/MRI field-strength details are not present in the extracted record, those are preferred (I5) and not required for inclusion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, and I4 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of cocaine users (stimulant class) vs healthy controls reporting whole-brain voxelwise GM volume results. NeuroStore extracts show whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference for between-group contrasts (HC>iCUD and iCUD>HC) with FDR-corrected results, and a within-patient longitudinal whole-brain contrast showing GM increases at follow-up. Participant demographics and substance-use status are reported. These meet the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria for empirical MRI GM comparisons and whole-brain between-group reporting. MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not reported in this document, but absence of those preferred details does not preclude inclusion.

This NeuroStore record reports an empirical voxel-based morphometry study comparing methamphetamine-dependent individuals (n=61) to controls (n=44) on gray matter density, with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference and explicit between-group results (abstract: controls > MA in bilateral insula and left middle frontal gyrus). Participant demographics and substance-use details (age, sex, abstinence, age of first use) are provided. Although MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not specified, I5 states these are preferred but not required. No ROI-only restriction applies and the study is empirical human MRI. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons between substance users (stimulant class) and controls.

This is an empirical voxel-based morphometry study comparing smokers and never-smokers (n=32) that reports whole-brain, between-group voxelwise analyses of gray matter density (smokers < never-smokers) with whole-brain inference and FWE correction. Participant demographics and substance-use measures (age, sex, cigarettes/day, FTND, pack-years, years of smoking) are reported. Coordinates/peaks are provided. Thus the study addresses the review objective (nicotine) and meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM comparison), I3 (whole-brain between-group GM contrast), I4 (results reported in extractable form), and I5 (participant and substance details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). The NeuroStore record appears complete for screening purposes, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study is an empirical VBM MRI study comparing gray matter volume between binge-drinking young adults and non-binge control subjects. NeuroStore data show at least one whole-brain between-group contrast (Analysis 24789323_analysis_1: model fit over = whole brain, BD > controls) reporting voxelwise results, satisfying the review’s whole-brain requirement. The paper reports participant age and sex details and substance-use characteristics. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM comparison), I3 (reports a whole-brain between-group GM contrast), I4 (voxelwise results are reported), and I5 (participant and substance details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical human structural MRI VBM study comparing smokers to matched controls. Analysis 20699124_analysis_0 reports whole-brain voxelwise gray matter density between high pack-years smokers and controls, with permutation-based FWE correction and reported peak coordinates (Table t0015). Participant age/sex and substance-use measures (pack-years, FTND) are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I2 (empirical GM MRI study), I3 (whole-brain between-group GM contrast), and I4 (coordinates/peaks reported). MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not listed in the provided record (I5 not fully satisfied), but that alone does not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of GM differences in substance users versus controls.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing cocaine-dependent individuals (stimulant users) to healthy controls using voxelwise whole-brain analyses of gray matter volume. The NeuroStore record shows whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference for between-group contrasts (controls > patients) with voxelwise FWE thresholding and peak coordinates reported in tables. Thus it meets: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences), I3 (reports at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls for GM), and I4 (voxelwise results reported as table peaks). Participant demographics and analysis software (SPM8) are reported, but MRI field strength was not specified; I5 is therefore partially but not fully documented (preferred only). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears available via the NeuroStore extraction, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Study is an empirical VBM structural MRI investigation comparing non-treatment-seeking cocaine-dependent individuals to healthy controls and reports at least one whole-brain between-group contrast (controls > cocaine users) with whole-brain inference. The population (cocaine dependence) falls within the stimulant drug class of interest. Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics are reported. Results include voxelwise whole-brain morphometric findings (reported peaks). The study is not ROI-only and is original empirical work. MRI field strength and preprocessing/software details are not provided in the NeuroStore extract, but I5 is a preferred (not mandatory) item and absence does not preclude inclusion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, and I4 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This VBM study reports within-sample correlations between GMV and AUDIT scores across a continuum of drinking severity rather than a whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users versus healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (voxelwise results reported in tables/peaks), I5 (participant age/sex and substance-use characteristics reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I2 (does not present an empirical whole-brain GM volume comparison between substance users and controls), I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls; analyses are within-group regression). Exclusion criteria met: none (E5 not met because whole-brain analyses were performed; E6 not applicable). Therefore the study does not satisfy the required between-group comparison criteria for the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

Exclusion applied: E5 (study reports only region-of-interest morphometric analysis with no whole-brain GM volume contrast). Inclusion met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences between nicotine-dependent participants and controls). Inclusion NOT met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group voxelwise GM volume contrast reported; morphometry analysis was ROI-only within the cerebellum), I4 (no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise GM results reported). Full text appears available in the record. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to provide whole-brain GM between-group results required by the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study (PLOS ONE) comparing gray matter volume between abstinent alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls. The NeuroStore record shows voxelwise whole-brain analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) with FWE-corrected voxel-level thresholds and reported peak coordinates for between-group contrasts (HCs > abstainers; HCs > relapsers). Participant demographics and substance-use measures are reported. These elements satisfy the review inclusion criteria for GM volume studies with whole-brain between-group contrasts (I2, I3), acceptable reporting of voxelwise results (I4), and reporting of participant characteristics (I5). No ROI-only or non-empirical exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study reporting voxel-based morphometry (gray matter volume) whole-brain between-group contrasts that directly compare cocaine-use disorder (a stimulant class) with healthy controls. Analysis 28150390_analysis_2 explicitly lists a whole-brain Healthy Comparison > Cocaine-Use Disorder contrast with permutation-based cluster FWE correction and reported peak coordinates (Table t2). Participant age/sex and comorbidity details are reported. Voxelwise results are reported in tables (peaks) and whole-brain inference was performed. These facts satisfy the review criteria for inclusion: I2 (empirical MRI GM study comparing users vs controls), I3 (at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls), I4 (voxelwise results reported in tables), and I5 (participant demographics and some substance-use/comorbidity details reported). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears sufficiently represented in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study reports an empirical VBM analysis comparing smokers (nicotine dependence) and nonsmokers with gray matter volume as the outcome (measure: gray matter volume). The morphometric analysis (Analysis 30456877_analysis_0) was modeled over the whole brain (model fit over: whole brain) and reports peak coordinates, indicating voxelwise whole-brain results are available. Participant demographics and smoking characteristics are reported. The study directly addresses nicotine-related GM differences and therefore meets the review objective. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; is empirical human MRI).

This is an empirical structural MRI study of heavy nicotine-dependent male smokers vs controls that reports gray matter volume analyses. NeuroStore shows whole-brain model fitting for GM (multivariate SVM analyses fitted over the whole brain with reported peak coordinates) and a VBM analysis (although VBM inference was ROI-restricted). The presence of whole-brain voxelwise classification results with reported peaks/tables satisfies the requirement for at least one whole-brain between-group GM contrast. Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics are reported. Therefore the study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria for GM whole-brain evidence and coordinate reporting.

The paper reports only within-group, voxelwise regression analyses in cocaine-dependent participants (n=43) associating years of use and weeks abstinent with gray matter volume; NeuroStore extraction indicates 'cross subject regression, within-group' and lists only patient participants. No whole-brain between-group contrasts comparing substance users versus drug-naïve controls are reported, so the study does not provide the required user-vs-control comparisons. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (participant age/sex and substance-use details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (does not present empirical between-group GM comparisons vs controls), I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls), I4 (no qualifying between-group voxelwise results reported/tabled). No exclusion criteria apply (E5 and E6 not met). Full text appears complete in the NeuroStore record.

Study reports an empirical structural MRI comparison of alcohol-dependent patients (n=74) versus healthy controls (n=43) measuring gray matter volume. NeuroStore extraction indicates a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast (healthy controls > patients) with cluster-level FWE correction and reported peak coordinates (Table 2). Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics are provided. These details satisfy the review’s requirements for whole-brain GM volume comparisons between substance users and controls.

This is an empirical MRI study comparing cocaine users and controls (I2 met). However, the NeuroStore extraction shows no whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast of substance users vs. controls for gray matter volume. The reported between-group analysis (group x N200 interaction) and other contrasts are restricted to a cingulate ROI; the only whole-brain model fit reported is a within-group (controls) regression, not a between-group GM comparison. Therefore the study effectively reports only ROI-based between-group results and lacks a qualifying whole-brain between-group GM contrast (violates I3; meets exclusion E5). Based on these facts, exclude.

The study reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group gray matter volume comparisons between cocaine-dependent patients (stimulant users) and healthy controls (Analysis 26786150_analysis_1: patients > controls, whole-brain model fit, peaks reported in Table 2). Coordinates/peaks are provided in tables, satisfying the reporting requirement. The sample and contrast directly address structural GM differences between substance users and controls (stimulants = relevant drug class). Although voxelwise results are uncorrected (P<0.005, cluster extent 50), the study nonetheless provides whole-brain GMV comparisons and tables of peaks. Some preferred methodological details (e.g., MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are not explicitly reported in the NeuroStore extract, but I5 is stated as preferred and missing details alone do not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply.

The study investigates synthetic cannabinoid users and reports reduced grey matter in the abstract, but the provided NeuroStore record contains only voxelwise functional (BOLD) N-back contrasts and no whole-brain voxelwise structural GM volume analyses or coordinate tables for VBM. No exclusion criteria from the review (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) are explicitly met in the document. Therefore the study cannot be included because it does not provide the required whole-brain structural GM results (I3, I4).

This is an empirical structural MRI study reporting whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts comparing substance users and non-users (Analysis 24920451_analysis_1: no SUD > SUD), with gray matter volume as the outcome and reported peak coordinates (4 peaks). Therefore I2, I3, and I4 are satisfied; I5 (preferred reporting items) is not fully satisfied based on the document. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply.

The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group morphometric contrasts comparing alcohol users and healthy controls and reports grey-matter volumetric reductions in medial-prefrontal and orbitofrontal cortices in the abstract, with coordinate peaks available. NeuroStore notes model fit and inference over the whole brain and reports peaks (tables) for between-group contrasts, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise evidence. The study therefore meets the meta-analysis objective (GM differences between substance users and controls) and inclusion criteria I2, I3, and I4. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses or non-empirical paper) are met. This is an empirical VBM structural MRI study comparing alcohol use disorder (AUD) patients to healthy controls and reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (AUDs < HCs) with model fit and inference over the whole brain (voxel-level FDR). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical).

This study reports empirical, English-language structural MRI morphometric comparisons of gray matter between cocaine-dependent participants and healthy controls (meets I2). It includes at least one whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast (CON > CUD) with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference, thresholding, and reported peak coordinates/tables (meets I3 and I4). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not an ROI-only study nor a non-empirical paper. The sample is male, cocaine users (stimulant class) vs controls, directly addressing the review objective of identifying GM differences for stimulants. Therefore the paper should be included.

The study should be excluded under E5. Although it addresses the review objective for stimulants and includes an empirical structural MRI morphometry contrast (Controls > CUD) (I2 satisfied) and reports voxelwise peaks (Reported peaks: Table t4, so I4 satisfied), the morphometric analysis was conducted and reported only within region(s) of interest (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest). Because it reports only ROI-based structural results with no qualifying whole-brain GM between-group results, it meets exclusion criterion E5 and must be excluded.

This is an empirical voxel-based morphometry MRI study comparing gray matter density between alcohol-dependent patients (n=20) and controls (n=20) using whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (Control > Alcoholics). Full text is available as represented by the record.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent participants to healthy controls using whole-brain voxelwise surface-based morphometry (cortical thickness) with Talairach coordinates and peak tables reported. This study reports an empirical VBM analysis comparing gray matter volume between individuals with cocaine use disorder and healthy controls. This NeuroStore record reports an empirical MRI study comparing cannabis-dependent individuals (n=89) to matched controls (n=89) with whole-brain morphometric analyses. It reports a whole-brain, vertex-wise two-sample t-test for cortical thickness with whole-brain inference (reported peak), and voxelwise whole-white-matter skeleton diffusion results; the cortical thickness result constitutes a whole-brain between-group GM contrast relevant to the review objective. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM differences) and I3 (reports at least one whole-brain between-group GM contrast). I4 is satisfied because voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain results and reported peaks are available. Exclusion E5 applies: the NeuroStore record reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses and multivariate classification using cortical ROI features (1,024 ROIs); no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast of smokers vs. nonsmokers is reported. This study addresses alcohol dependence and reports voxel-based morphometry measures of gray matter asymmetry (meets I2). Participant demographics and substance-use details are reported (meets I5). The study reports original empirical structural MRI morphometric data comparing alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls (meets I2). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not an ROI-only analysis (E5) nor non-empirical (E6). Therefore the study addresses the review objective (alcohol as one of the substance classes) and provides qualifying whole-brain GM differences for inclusion.

This study does not address the required between-group comparison of substance users vs controls. The record does report whole-brain voxelwise results and participant/covariate information, but these do not satisfy the meta-analysis requirement. Exclusion IDs met: none (E5 and E6 do not apply).

The study reports empirical VBM and DTI data in an English-language PLoS One article comparing detoxified alcohol-dependent men to healthy controls. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and should be included in the meta-analysis of grey-matter volume differences between substance users and controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of heroin-dependent patients on methadone maintenance (opioid users) comparing gray matter volume between 27 MMT patients and 23 healthy controls. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be INCLUDED.

This study reports empirical voxelwise whole-brain structural MRI comparisons of grey matter between smokers and never-smokers (n=45; 22 smokers, 23 never-smokers). This study reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group analyses comparing gray matter volume in alcohol-dependent patients (ADP) versus healthy controls (HC). Analysis 28992531_analysis_2 explicitly states GM volume reductions (HC > ADP) with model fit and inference over the whole brain and 20 reported peaks, meeting the requirement for whole-brain between-group GM contrasts. MRI field strength and preprocessing/software are not stated in the NeuroStore record but I5 is described as preferred and missing details do not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI analyses or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the paper should be included.

This study reports whole-brain voxelwise structural MRI analyses comparing alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls (between-group contrast: Controls > Patients) assessing gray matter volume, with FWE-corrected peaks and coordinate tables. This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) study comparing grey matter volume between smokers and healthy controls (nicotine dependence). However, I3 NOT met: the NeuroStore extraction reports a cross-subject regression (positive correlation with metacognitive accuracy) across patients and healthy participants, not an explicit whole-brain between-group contrast directly comparing substance users versus controls for GM volume. The meta-analysis requires at least one whole-brain between-group GM volume contrast (substance users vs controls). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses) apply. Full text appears complete in the provided record (fulltext_incomplete=false). Consequently the paper is excluded because it does not report the required whole-brain group comparison (I3 missing).

The study used VBM to compare gray matter volume in alcohol-dependent patients versus controls, but NeuroStore extraction shows the analysis was fit over a region-of-interest and inference was restricted to that ROI (RFT-based FWE small-volume correction). This study reports a structural gray-matter analysis (Analysis 24258223_analysis_0) that is limited to a region-of-interest (contralateral rACC ROI) with region-level inference. This is an empirical, English VBM MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent patients to healthy controls (alcohol is one of the review’s target drug classes). This study reports whole-brain, between-group comparisons of smokers versus never-smokers but uses cortical thickness (structural morphometry) rather than GM volume/density/concentration measures specified in inclusion criterion I2. The NeuroStore record shows only within-group, cross-subject voxelwise regression analyses relating substance use measures to GM volume (negative correlations). The study is an empirical, English-language structural MRI VBM study comparing adolescents with DSM-IV alcohol dependence (n=58) to matched healthy controls (n=58). This study reports structural morphometry (gray matter volume) comparisons between alcohol-dependent patients and controls (meets I2) and provides coordinate peaks in tables (meets I4). This is an empirical structural MRI study of adolescents with alcohol use disorder (meets I2). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons between substance users and controls and is INCLUDED.

This study examined associations between AUDIT score and grey matter using whole-brain voxelwise and surface analyses in a large sample (N=436) and reports coordinates; participant age/sex and other details are provided. However, the analyses are cross-subject regressions (within-group associations with AUD severity) rather than whole-brain between-group contrasts comparing substance users versus controls. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI studies assessing GM differences between substance users and controls) nor I3 (must report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (acceptable reporting of voxelwise results) and I5 (participant demographics and substance use details reported). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete in the provided record.

The NeuroStore record reports an empirical structural MRI study comparing gray matter volume between alcoholic patients and healthy controls. It includes a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain; FWE-corrected results reported) for gray matter morphometry with reported peak coordinates. Participant demographics and substance-use details are provided; statistical model (ANCOVA with TIV and age covariates) is described. These elements satisfy the review’s requirements for empirical GM volume comparisons and qualifying whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears accessible via the NeuroStore extraction, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This study reports diffusion MRI (white-matter) metrics comparing adolescent initiators vs non-initiators; the meta-analysis requires empirical studies of grey matter (GM) volume differences. Although the paper reports whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates (Table t3) and provides participant age/sex and other metadata, it does not assess GM volume/density/concentration. Therefore it does not meet the critical inclusion criteria for GM outcomes and whole-brain GM contrasts.

This study examines structural grey-matter morphology (cortical thickness) in alcohol use disorder patients vs controls and reports peak coordinates in tables with participant age/sex details; thus it meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI study of grey-matter structural measures), I4 (results reported as peaks/tables), and I5 (participant and sample information reported). However, NeuroStore’s extraction explicitly states “Model fit over: region of interest” and “Thresholding: region-level” for all analyses, and there is no clear qualifying whole-brain voxelwise GM-volume contrast reported that compares substance users vs controls. Therefore it fails I3 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only results with no qualifying whole-brain results). Despite a label in individual analyses (“Whole-brain t test parameters”), the extracted model-fit and thresholding fields indicate ROI-restricted analyses. Result: EXCLUDED (E5).

The study examines gray matter differences between cocaine users and controls (meets I2) and reports participant demographics/substance characteristics (meets I5). However, the between-group morphometric analysis (healthy controls > CUD) had inference restricted to a region-of-interest (small-volume correction) despite model fitting over the whole brain. There is no qualifying whole-brain between-group voxelwise result reported — only ROI-restricted inference — so it does not satisfy the requirement for a whole-brain between-group contrast (I3). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only ROI-restricted between-group inference with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text is available in the provided record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest (small-volume) inference despite fitting models over the whole brain, meeting exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM differences between cannabis users and non-users) and I4 (voxelwise peak coordinates are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (does not provide a qualifying whole-brain between-group GM contrast—inference was restricted to ROI with FWE small-volume correction). The study therefore fails the required whole-brain evidence criterion and is excluded.

This study is an empirical structural MRI investigation of smoking (nicotine) and reports gray-matter density contrasts between smokers (successful/unsuccessful quitters) and never-smokers, with peak coordinates in a table — satisfying I2 (empirical MRI study of GM differences) and I4 (voxelwise results reported in tables). However, all reported analyses were fit over region-of-interest masks (Model fit over: region of interest; regions: UQ gray matter loss mask, SQ gray matter loss mask) with no indication of any whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrasts. Therefore it fails the required whole-brain evidence criterion (I3) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI analyses reported). Reporting of MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software is not provided in the record (I5 not fully met). Conclusion: EXCLUDED due to E5; inclusion criteria met: I2, I4; inclusion criteria not met: I3, I5.

This study is excluded because it does not provide whole-brain GM volume (e.g., VBM) comparisons between substance users and controls. The reported analyses are cortical thickness, gyrification (LGI), and other structural morphometry metrics, not GM volume/density/concentration (I2 not met). The contrasts are within patients (early-onset vs other users; interaction with years of MJ use) and there is no clear users vs control between-group GM volume contrast reported (I3 not met). The paper does report participant demographics and substance-use characteristics (I5 met). No exclusion criteria (E5,E6) apply. Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

This study is excluded because it does not report any comparisons of substance users versus healthy controls. The paper reports within-group voxelwise regressions (abstinence duration correlations) and between-group contrasts among patient subgroups (FLUs vs FRUs), but no whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users vs controls. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (voxelwise results/peaks reported in tables) and I5 (participant age and substance-use characteristics reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (does not assess GM differences between substance users and controls), I3 (no whole-brain between-group substance users vs controls contrast). No exclusion criteria from the review (E5, E6) are triggered. fulltext_incomplete=false.

The NeuroStore record does not report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast of gray matter (GM) volume/density. The extracted analyses describe a perfusion (cerebral blood flow) whole-brain cue-reactivity ANOVA; although the abstract mentions a decreased gray matter density in dlPFC, the document provides no whole-brain GM between-group analysis, coordinates, or table/figure evidence to satisfy the meta-analysis requirement. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I3 (no qualifying whole-brain GM contrast reported). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English MRI study; T1 data and GM density comment present). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain GM volume between-group contrast reported), I4 (no voxelwise GM results reported in tables/figures in this record). No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI analyses) can be confirmed from the provided document. Based on the provided record, exclude.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study of cocaine-dependent patients vs healthy controls assessing gray matter density using voxelwise morphometry. The NeuroStore record shows whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference for between-group contrasts (controls > patients) with reported peak coordinates (tables), participant demographics (n, age, sex) and substance-use characteristics. These elements satisfy the review objective (structural GM differences for a stimulant) and meet inclusion criteria: I2 (empirical MRI GM study), I3 (at least one whole-brain between-group GM contrast), I4 (voxelwise results reported in coordinate tables), and I5 (participant age/sex and substance-use details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears available via the derived record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical, English-language voxel-based morphometry MRI study that directly compares grey matter volume between substance users (polysubstance use disorder) and healthy controls. The analysis reports whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference for between-group contrasts with Talairach coordinates and a table of reported peaks, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics are provided (n=76, ages, male-only, duration of use, and 40 stimulant users), so the study is relevant to the meta-analysis objective (includes stimulant users among polysubstance users). MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software are not reported, but missing these details does not preclude inclusion per the protocol. Therefore inclusion criteria I2, I3, and I4 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The paper reports an fMRI study with a VBM analysis restricted to the (para)hippocampal region (abstract: ‘VBM-analysis of the (para)hippocampal regions’), and the NeuroStore record contains only a whole-brain functional contrast. No whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM volume contrast or coordinates are reported. Therefore the study does not provide the required whole-brain structural GM comparisons (I3) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only structural analysis). It does meet I2 (empirical English MRI study comparing GM between users and controls via VBM) and I5 (participant age/sex reported). Full text appears accessible in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study examines cortical thickness (structural morphometry) rather than GM volume/density/concentration measures required by the review. Although it reports whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance (alcohol/DWI) offenders vs controls with whole-brain inference and peak coordinates (satisfying I3 and I4) and reports participant characteristics (I5), it does not assess GM volume differences as specified in I2. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study is excluded for failing inclusion criterion I2.

This study examines cortical thickness (surface-based morphometry) rather than grey matter volume/density/concentration as specified by inclusion criterion I2. Although it reports whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing binge drinkers (BD) and light drinkers (LD) with coordinate peaks (satisfying I3 and I4) and provides participant sex and substance-use measures (satisfying I5), it does not assess GM volume differences (I2 not met). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only analyses, empirical MRI data present). Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to meet the required I2 criterion.

This is an empirical human structural MRI morphometry study comparing binge-drinking (BD) participants to healthy volunteers (HV). It reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group analyses: Analysis 26900571_analysis_2 is a group-by-gender interaction with model fit and inference over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates (Table t0010). Grey matter volume is the measure, and participant age/sex and substance-use severity (AUDIT) are reported. MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software are not shown in the NeuroStore extract, but I5 is explicitly described as preferred (not mandatory). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM volume comparisons between substance users (alcohol binge drinkers) and controls.

Exclusion E5 applied: the study reports gray matter comparisons only within an a priori hippocampal ROI (Analysis 15607838_analysis_0; small-volume correction) and does not present any whole-brain between-group gray-matter (GM) contrast. While the paper does report whole-brain voxelwise between-group analyses, those whole-brain results are for white-matter density (Analyses 15607838_analysis_2 and _3). Inclusion criterion I2 is met (empirical English MRI study assessing GM differences between substance users and controls). Inclusion criterion I3 is NOT met (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported). Inclusion criterion I4 (acceptability of voxelwise results reported in tables/figures) is not sufficient to rescue inclusion because the qualifying voxelwise results required by I3 are absent for GM. Therefore the study must be excluded under E5.

The NeuroStore record reports an empirical structural MRI study comparing gray matter between cannabis users and healthy controls with at least one whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast (Analysis 21050680_analysis_0: healthy controls > cannabis users, model fit over whole brain, GM volume). Voxelwise coordinates/peaks are reported, and additional regression analyses relating THC/CBD and CBD to hippocampal GM are present (one ROI-restricted analysis does not preclude inclusion because whole-brain between-group results are reported). Participant age/sex and substance-use exclusions are provided. Therefore the study meets the review objective and the inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM differences between substance users and controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI VBM study comparing grey matter volume between cannabis users and non-users (n=88). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (model fit and inference over whole brain) using SPM8, with coordinate peaks reported in tables and cluster-level FWE thresholding. Participant age/sex and substance-use characteristics are reported; preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) is specified (MRI field strength not reported, but absence does not exclude). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

The NeuroStore record reports voxelwise VBM correlations between grey matter volume and behavioral measures across a sample of binge drinkers and healthy volunteers, but does not report any whole-brain between-group comparison of substance users versus controls (no direct GM volume contrast: binge drinkers vs controls). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (voxelwise results/coordinates are reported) and I5 (participant age/sex and substance-use characteristics are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (the paper does not present a between-group GM volume comparison between substance users and controls as required by I2) and I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls is reported). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet required inclusion criteria I2 and I3.
